## Scope

This repository is one GETQUICK Site: its features, its site-owned files and
its own decisions. The blueprint (`gq-site`), GETQUICK plugins and packages,
and platform-wide decisions (`gq-platform`) each live in their own repository
([gq-platform ADR 0001](https://github.com/Quick-Release/gq-platform/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-ownership-of-work-across-getquick-repositories.md)).

Before acting on a request, ask "whose release would ship this?". Read any
repository for evidence, but change only this one: its code, issues and PRs.
When a request belongs to another repository, change nothing anywhere. Reply
with that repository (`Quick-Release/<name>` and its local clone) and tell the
user to start a new session there, in a worktree of that repository. When the
owner is unclear, point to Quick-Release/gq-platform the same way. This applies
even when the change looks small, or when this session already has the other
repository's context.

## Managed files

This site follows the GETQUICK blueprint, the shared tooling published as
[`@getquick/site`](https://github.com/Quick-Release/gq-site) (the `gq`
command), pinned to an exact version in the root `devDependencies`. Its
ownership manifest (`node_modules/@getquick/site/blueprint/ownership.json`)
lists what `gq sync` manages here: whole files, this section of `AGENTS.md`
and one of `.gitignore`, and keys of the root `package.json` (the toolchain
pins, the hook install and the scripts that wrap `gq`). `gq.lock.json`
records what `gq` last wrote.

- Don't edit managed output by hand: `gq sync` stops with a diff when it
  finds an edit. Fix the template in `@getquick/site`, publish a release, bump
  the pin, then run `gq sync` (`gq sync --check` reports what is pending).
- Site guidance goes in `AGENTS.md` outside this section, and site ignore
  rules in `.gitignore` outside its section; both survive every sync.
- Create-once files, such as `GLOSSARY.md` and `README.md`, are the site's
  once written: `gq sync` never rewrites or restores them unless asked to
  with `gq sync --recreate <path>`.
- Anything the manifest doesn't list is site-owned and never touched.

## Safety

- Never commit plaintext `.env`, `.env.local`, `.dev.vars`, Composer
  `auth.json`, salts, API tokens, or deployment credentials.
- Secrets are managed through Sigillo (`gq.ops.json`, `gq sigillo`), not
  committed `.env` files. Never run `sigillo secrets download --force` or
  `sigillo run --mount`, and never bulk-copy a full Sigillo environment into
  Cloudflare or Ploi — inject secrets per command/deploy through
  `gq sigillo run <environment> -- <command>` instead.
  Public `PUBLIC_*`/`VITE_*` values stay in checked config, not Sigillo.
- Treat Ploi and production WordPress as deployment targets, not development
  databases.
- Database synchronization is one-way, production to local: `pnpm db:sync`
  (`gq db sync`) backs the live database up to R2 (`gq.ops.json`
  `backups`), imports it into DDEV, search-replaces the URLs and resets the
  local `dev`/`dev` admin (`local.adminEmail`). Never push a local database
  to Ploi, and never add a command that does, here or in `@getquick/site`:
  the only script `db:sync` sends to Ploi is the export, and the package's
  export-only guard refuses anything that can write to a database.
- Use Sigillo locally or the protected CI secret store for Cloudflare
  credentials; do not place them in source files or deployment configuration.

## Docs

[`docs/`](docs/) holds ADRs, research write-ups, migration plans, and
agent-facing reference docs — see each subdirectory's `README.md` for the
convention. It starts empty; add to it as real decisions/research
accumulate, don't pre-fill it with speculative content.

## Agent skills

Project skills live in [`.agents/skills/`](.agents/skills/), the single
source for every agent: pi reads it natively, and `.claude/skills` is a
committed symlink to it for Claude Code. Add or edit skills there only —
don't recreate `.pi/skills` or a real `.claude/skills` directory.

### Issue tracker

Issues and specs live in GitHub Issues, managed with the `gh` CLI. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Use `needs-triage`, `needs-info`, `ready-for-agent`, `ready-for-human`, and `wontfix`. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Use the single-context layout with root `GLOSSARY.md` and `docs/adr/`. See `docs/agents/domain.md`.
